info.corpo: 2,678 points. Top 40 out of 166 albums nominated by bloggers, radio hosts and journalists of the heavy underground.
Roadburn Chronicles debuts at #14 in the August 2026 Doom Charts, published September 4.
Roadburn Chronicles, out August 28, 2026 on Octopus Rising / Argonauta Records.
The extended groove of stoner rock. The crushing weight of classic doom. High-voltage fuzz, hypnotic tempos.
Toxic Basement Studio, Carate Brianza, with Carlo Altobelli. November 2024 to January 2025: tubes, drum room, valve saturation.
Roadburn Chronicles crosses four dimensions of the self: the shadow we absorb, the illusions that collapse, the change that costs before it heals, and the love, freedom and loss that follow.
Revenant has an official video on YouTube. Viper, as Inner-Strength Check puts it, is one of the darkest sides of the album.
A sub-label of Argonauta Records, the Italian home of stoner, doom, sludge and post metal. Distribution across Europe, the Americas and Japan.
01 S.U.R.E. / 02 The Sinner / 03 Turning Point / 04 I For An I / 05 Rusty Blues / 06 Viper / 07 Revenant / 08 Dreamer's Sunsets / 09 Monsters' Conceal / 10 An Old Van and a Couple of Beers

info.titolo: This is how weight is built.
info.corpo: Guitar with active pickups, Orange tube head, 5-string bass tuned low. British and vintage fuzz.
An old blue van crosses a psychedelic desert. The last track on the record is 'An Old Van and a Couple of Beers'.
A bench, a toast for Father's Day. A dirty, deep blues, as Radiocoop describes it.
Radiocoop also hears Motörhead-style speed metal (I For An I) and dirty, deep blues (Rusty Blues).

info.titolo: The name that keeps coming back: Kyuss.
info.corpo: Outlaws Of The Sun and Pitstop Metal cite it among the influences. In the Breathing The Core interview, Kyuss is among the reference points named by the band.
Cited by the press: Kyuss, Orange Goblin, Dozer, Monster Magnet, Fu Manchu. (Outlaws Of The Sun, Pitstop Metal)

info.titolo: The press puts them side by side.
info.corpo: Kyuss, Orange Goblin and Dozer according to Steve Howe of Outlaws Of The Sun. Monster Magnet and Fu Manchu are also cited by Pitstop Metal.
In the EPK's FFO: The Sword, Black Sabbath, Windhand, Down, Trouble.
The Petrosa repertoire adapts to the occasion: a tight opening slot or a full-length show.
Short slot or headline night: we build the set around your event.
Tube amps, fuzz and a rhythm section that moves the room.
Roadburn Chronicles played live: bigger riffs, more air moved.

A live show made to be felt: stoner and doom from Milan, Italy.
Recorded, mixed and mastered by Carlo Altobelli at Toxic Basement Studio in Carate Brianza.
Eight days of sessions between November 2024 and January 2025, with an analog live approach.
Roadburn Chronicles is out on Octopus Rising / Argonauta Records. 51 minutes of stoner/doom from Milan.
Petrosa formed in 2019. Roadburn Chronicles, out August 28, 2026, is their debut album.
The wide groove of stoner rock meets the crushing weight of classic doom.
High-voltage fuzz and considered tempo changes. Stoner/doom from Milan.

info.titolo: Crossing the shadow to find yourself.
info.corpo: Ten songs, one throughline: the sinner, the judge, the rebel, the wounded lover and the grieving son all belong to the same consciousness. Not a clean win of light over darkness, a harder reconciliation with all of it.
Revenant and Viper. Then play the record all the way through.
The debut is out on Octopus Rising / Argonauta Records, on streaming and on CD.

info.titolo: It ends on a road song.
info.corpo: The last track is An Old Van and a Couple of Beers.

band.corpo: Guitar and founder. Ex-Orphean (death metal), he started Petrosa in 2019.
Massive tube-driven riffs, pentatonic grooves, British and vintage fuzz. The architect of the Petrosa sound.
Drums. Milanese, raised on skate culture and squat-scene punk.
Dynamic control, dry snare, heavy ride and crash. The engine that drives the weight.
Vocals. Baritone with over twenty years of experience: from clean to distorted.
Bluesy grit, authoritative melody, cavernous doom timbre. The emotional heart of the band.
Bass. After Big Crunch, in Petrosa since 2024.
Thick, sinister tone, clean sub-lows, overdrive in the mids. It amplifies every riff.

Founded by Antonio Buonocore. Now four strong: Antonio, Giorgio, Aldo and Andrea.

analyses.caption:
Self Utopias Ruins Existence.

S.U.R.E. opens with questions that refuse to comfort: "Do you see light with your closed eyes?" "Do you feel safe enough with your closed ears?" "Do you feel like a prophet with your evil tongue?" Closed eyes, closed ears, a destructive tongue: three ways of shutting the world out while calling it certainty.

Then the warning grows teeth: "Anger is an acid that can do more harm to the fucking vessel in which it is stored than to anything on which it is poured." Rage promises power over an enemy, and corrodes the one carrying it first. "You're dying in silence between slaves'n'Rulers" is the price of picking a side and calling it safety.

The title spells it out: Self Utopias Ruins Existence. The perfect stories we build about ourselves can start as protection and end as prisons.

Our reading of the lyrics. S.U.R.E. is track 01 on Roadburn Chronicles. Stream it on Spotify (link in bio).

Which certainty are you most afraid to question?

parts.titolo: Bin of morality and rotten diamonds.
parts.corpo: S.U.R.E. opens on a landscape already spoiled: "Bin of morality and rotten diamonds. Stormy winds when the fog rises." Before any accusation lands, the ground is already unstable.

parts.titolo: Are you aware that you're dying?
parts.corpo: Three questions repeat like a diagnosis: closed eyes, closed ears, an evil tongue. Each one asks the same thing back: "Are you aware that You're dying?" Not a threat, an alarm.

parts.titolo: Pillars of sand: the right, the true.
parts.corpo: "Pillars of sand, The right, the true, the false and the God, An anthill and the Colosseum." Whole systems of certainty, reduced to something that can't hold weight.

parts.titolo: Anger is an acid.
parts.corpo: "Anger is an acid that can do more harm to the fucking vessel in which it is stored than to anything on which it is poured." Rage promises power over an enemy. It corrodes the one holding it first.

parts.titolo: You're dying in silence.
parts.corpo: "You're dying in silence between slaves'n'Rulers." Picking a side and calling it safety has a cost: it just relocates the silence.

parts.titolo: A simple sum that shakes the mountains.
parts.corpo: "Such a simple sum that shakes the mountains, It floods every groove and kills the question." Certainty is efficient. It also stops the asking.

parts.titolo: Self Utopias Ruins Existence.
parts.corpo: The title spells out the diagnosis: Self Utopias Ruins Existence. The perfect stories we build about ourselves can start as protection and end as a prison we built with our own hands.

parts.titolo: Part of a bigger fracture.
parts.corpo: S.U.R.E. tears down the certainties we perform for the world. I For An I turns the same blade inward, into the argument between the voices that built them. Together they're the record's full account of an illusion collapsing, from the outside in and the inside out.

analyses.caption:
Judgment becomes identity.

The Sinner opens with a list of self-condemning identities: "I'm a sinner, an enemy of God, family ruiner, a demon of my time." They sound like accusations from outside, until the song reveals they've been absorbed as truth: "My way is mapped out, between fog, dust and rivers."

Then the turn: "And I'm here now, with all my colors, the only one awake among my enemies." Freedom begins when the protagonist stops dividing the acceptable self from the self he was told to hide. The final blow still lands inward: "an enemy of myself."

Our reading of the lyrics. The Sinner is track 02 on Roadburn Chronicles. Stream it on Spotify (link in bio).

Which part of yourself have you been told to hide?

parts.titolo: I'm a sinner, an enemy of God.
parts.corpo: The Sinner opens with a list of verdicts: "I'm a sinner, an enemy of God, Family ruiner, A demon of my time." They read like accusations from outside, until you notice who's speaking them.

parts.titolo: My way is mapped out.
parts.corpo: "So let it be, Let it be done, My way is mapped out, Between fog, dust and rivers." Fog is uncertainty, dust is mortality, rivers are time. An interior landscape, not a road.

parts.titolo: Grey like my skies, purple like my veins.
parts.corpo: "Grey like my skies, And purple like my veins, Any color you prefer, They're just a part of me." The self stops being one thing. It becomes a whole palette, contradictions included.

parts.titolo: Past, present and future: all chaotic.
parts.corpo: "I don't know what I see, It's all chaotic, Past present and future." Guilt collapses time: what happened keeps inhabiting the present and colors everything still to come.

parts.titolo: And I'm here now, with all my colors.
parts.corpo: "And I'm here now, with all my colors, the only one awake among my enemies." The emotional center of the song: freedom starts when he stops hiding half of himself.

parts.titolo: The Earth is calling my body.
parts.corpo: "Future is clear now, Like water I drank, The Earth is calling my body, And stone reveals my name." Acceptance arrives as something almost physical, gravity instead of relief.

parts.titolo: An enemy of myself.
parts.corpo: The final turn lands inward: "Cause I'm the sinner, An enemy of myself, A demon of my Life." The harshest tribunal was never external. It was always self-judgment.

parts.titolo: The other half of the shadow.
parts.corpo: The Sinner ends in acceptance: every color finally worn at once. Viper is the warning about what that same acceptance can curdle into, one track later, when the shadow stops being carried and starts being craved.

analyses.caption:
Change costs before it heals.

Turning Point opens with a contradiction: "In the greenest meadows breath is poisonous." A life that looks fertile from outside can be uninhabitable within. The "Compass has been broken for long time," and the real question isn't how it happened, but "What will you do now?"

The shift itself is quiet: "Do you feel it? Your wind is changing." Nothing around the singer necessarily moves. The direction does. Growth is "the hardest sowing, the precious yield": "You tasted the mud, tastes like the blood," and none of it is wasted.

By the end: "It's finally dawn." Not proof the night never happened, proof it wasn't the whole story.

Our reading of the lyrics. Turning Point is track 03 on Roadburn Chronicles. Stream it on Spotify (link in bio).

What told you your wind was changing?

parts.titolo: In the greenest meadows, breath is poisonous.
parts.corpo: Turning Point opens on a contradiction: "In the greenest meadows breath is poisonous." A life that looks fertile from outside can be uninhabitable within.

parts.titolo: Compass has been broken for long time.
parts.corpo: "Compass has been broken for long time, You couldn't know why you never wanted to." The real question isn't how it happened. It's "What will you do now?"

parts.titolo: Do you feel it? Your wind is changing.
parts.corpo: "Do you feel it? Your wind is changing, One single moment, A turning Point." Nothing around him necessarily moves. The direction does, and that's the whole song.

parts.titolo: The hardest sowing, the precious yield.
parts.corpo: "The hardest sowing, The precious yield, A necessary and lonely hard path, Never gratitude." Growth here isn't rewarded. It's paid for, alone, on credit.

parts.titolo: You tasted the mud, tastes like the blood.
parts.corpo: "More effort and more pain, You tasted the mud, Tastes like the blood." The cost is physical, almost literal, nothing about this turning point is gentle.

parts.titolo: Times you killed, times you hurt.
parts.corpo: "The edge of sunset is hiding traces of times you killed, of times you hurt." Even light carries evidence. Nothing gets erased, only carried forward.

parts.titolo: It's finally dawn.
parts.corpo: "It's finally dawn, So much poison'n'mud, An elusive and shining light." Dawn doesn't cancel the night. It proves the night wasn't the whole story.

parts.titolo: Where the turn leads.
parts.corpo: Turning Point pays for change slowly, in mud and blood, with nothing applauding it. Revenant is what happens when that same change arrives all at once instead: total collapse, then something rising out of the wreckage.

analyses.caption:
A civil war fought in one head.

I For An I sets two voices against each other. One is the internal judge: "Old one, old one, how sad you are," demanding obedience and gratitude. The other is younger and unruly: "Careful boy," dreaming of roads and freedom the judge calls dangerous.

Neither side wins, because neither is complete: "We have the same fucking weight. One blind, one deaf." They despise each other and need each other in equal measure, locked in the same body, memory and history.

The exit the singer chooses isn't certainty, it's honesty: "I prefer doubt and fear." Not comfortable. Still alive.

Our reading of the lyrics. I For An I is track 04 on Roadburn Chronicles. Stream it on Spotify (link in bio).

Which voice is louder in your head today?

parts.titolo: Careful boy, dreaming of roads and freedom.
parts.corpo: I For An I opens with a warning voice: "Careful boy, Oh You can't think, Dreaming of roads and freedom, Wrong about life." Freedom, from this mouth, sounds like a diagnosis.

parts.titolo: Baby, I need you, I need it!
parts.corpo: "Baby oh you're just a joke, but I need you, I need it! Rambling and rambling you wrong, but I want it too, I need it!" Contempt and need, in the same breath, the mask slips early.

parts.titolo: Old one, old one, how sad you are.
parts.corpo: The younger voice answers back: "Old one, old one, how sad you are, Seeing so much agony, I see the rot between your teeth." Authority, seen up close, looks exhausted.

parts.titolo: I smell the stench of silent life.
parts.corpo: "I smell the stench of silent life, Monochromatic words yeah, You're teaching me while truth chokes you." An existence drained of color by inherited formulas.

parts.titolo: We have the same fucking weight.
parts.corpo: "We have the same fucking weight, One blind, one deaf." Neither voice wins, because neither is complete. They're locked together by the very thing they argue about.

parts.titolo: This isn't my fucking role.
parts.corpo: "This isn't my fucking role" is a refusal of the part he's been assigned, judge or rebel, obedient son or parasite. Neither fits.

parts.titolo: I prefer doubt and fear.
parts.corpo: The song closes on a choice, repeated three times: "I prefer doubt and fear." Not comfortable. Doubt keeps the question alive; fear proves something still matters.

parts.titolo: The war behind the walls.
parts.corpo: S.U.R.E. tears down the certainties we build for the world to see. I For An I is that same demolition turned inward, fought between two voices sharing one skull. Neither song lets the other one off easy.

analyses.caption:
Grief that still gets a toast.

Rusty Blues sits on a bench that isn't empty anymore: "Your bench ain't empty anymore, young folks and families pass by." But at night, the conversation resumes: "But when night falls and darkness creeps, I sit and I can talk to you." A small ritual keeps the bond alive: "A sip of wine, a toast for Father's Day."

The grief isn't only for what's gone, it's for everything still ahead that can't be witnessed: "You're missing out on this world and on my life too." Even the city changes shape: "The city feels so empty and strange since you've been gone one summer's night."

The last image holds the whole contradiction of mourning: "And when I meet some old white-haired man, I hope it's you, I hope, I'm wrong."

Our reading of the lyrics. Rusty Blues is track 05 on Roadburn Chronicles. Stream it on Spotify (link in bio).

Who would you still talk to, if you could?

parts.titolo: Your bench ain't empty anymore.
parts.corpo: Rusty Blues opens on a bench that fills with strangers: "Your bench ain't empty anymore, Young folks and families pass by." Life keeps moving around the empty seat.

parts.titolo: I sit and I can talk to you.
parts.corpo: "But when night falls and darkness creeps, I sit and I can talk to you." The need to speak survives whether or not anyone can still listen.

parts.titolo: A toast for Father's Day.
parts.corpo: "A sip of wine, A toast for Father's Day, Red and sparkling wine." A small, repeatable ritual, the kind that keeps a relationship honest longer than any big speech would.

parts.titolo: You're missing out on this world.
parts.corpo: "You're missing out on this world and on my life too." The grief isn't only for what's gone. It's for everything ahead that can no longer be witnessed.

parts.titolo: Another one, son. Those were the days.
parts.corpo: "I remember how you'd look and say, Another one, son, Those were the days!" Memory keeps a voice, a phrase, the exact texture of a moment already over.

parts.titolo: The city feels so empty and strange.
parts.corpo: "The city feels so empty and strange since you've been gone one summer's night." Even the streets change shape once one specific person stops walking them.

parts.titolo: I hope it's you, I hope, I'm wrong.
parts.corpo: The closing image holds the whole contradiction of mourning: "And when I meet some old white-haired man, I hope it's you, I hope, I'm wrong." Recognition and reason, arguing at once.

parts.titolo: One thread among several.
parts.corpo: Rusty Blues carries the album's quietest kind of love, the kind that keeps a small ritual alive long after there's a reason to. It belongs beside Monsters' Conceal, Dreamer's Sunsets and the open road of the closing track: the record's long look at love, freedom and loss.

analyses.caption:
The poison is sweet. That's the danger.

Viper doesn't open with pain, it opens with pleasure: "Create toxin. I tasted it. So sweet!" Toxic love rarely announces itself as destruction. It arrives as intensity, recognition, a bond unlike any other: "My perversion, your innocence are the elements."

Then the craving takes hold: "You're vibrating for the bite of Viper. And you are squealing for the bite of Viper." Year by year, "Skin is right now polluted by sin," and even after it ends, "Toxin leaves behind a splinter."

The hardest part isn't being bitten. It's still wanting the bite after you've named the venom.

Our reading of the lyrics. Viper is track 06 on Roadburn Chronicles. Stream it on Spotify (link in bio).

Have you ever wanted the bite more than the cure?

parts.titolo: Create toxin. I tasted it. So sweet!
parts.corpo: Viper doesn't open with pain, it opens with pleasure: "Create toxin, I tasted it. So sweet!" Toxic love rarely announces itself as destruction.

parts.titolo: My perversion, your innocence.
parts.corpo: "My perversion, your innocence are the elements, A lying process in between." Two people, not one villain and one victim, the toxin needs both.

parts.titolo: Isolation, exile.
parts.corpo: The warning arrives early and gets ignored anyway: "Isolation, exile, Or you will have to expect hate, regret, side effects." The danger is named. The pull stays stronger.

parts.titolo: Vibrating for the bite of Viper.
parts.corpo: "You're vibrating for the bite of Viper, And you are squealing for the bite of Viper." Craving and fear, sung in the same key.

parts.titolo: Skin is right now polluted by sin.
parts.corpo: "Year by year and piece by piece, Skin is right now polluted by sin." Toxic love rarely destroys in one strike. It changes the baseline, slowly, until it feels normal.

parts.titolo: Toxin leaves behind a splinter.
parts.corpo: "Toxin leaves behind a splinter, Sometimes it burn, sometimes it hurt." Even after it's over, something stays lodged where the bite was.

parts.titolo: Now I see their blinded faces.
parts.corpo: "Now I see their blinded faces, And now I understand their perturbations." Recognition arrives too late to prevent anything, only late enough to finally understand it.

parts.titolo: Where The Sinner's peace turns to hunger.
parts.corpo: The Sinner learns to carry every part of himself without apology. Viper is that same darkness one step further down the road: no longer carried, now craved. Acceptance and addiction, closer together than either song admits.

analyses.caption:
Freedom doesn't cancel death. It answers it.

Revenant opens on collapse: "Slowly creeps, Iron burns skin, Visions tear and absolutes fall." Truth bleeds, freedom fades, and still: "The Darkness is deep, But spirit stands tall."

The chorus turns collapse into ritual: "Taste my blood, rise again, serpent sun." The apocalyptic images around it, "Shattered moon, the veil is torn, Serpents fill the sky above," make the outer world a mirror of what's falling apart inside.

Then the key line: "Freedom defies death's embrace." Not a denial of the ending, "And from beginning, the end is known." A choice to keep walking anyway.

Our reading of the lyrics. Revenant is track 07 on Roadburn Chronicles. Stream it on Spotify (link in bio).

What keeps you standing when everything else falls?

parts.titolo: Slowly creeps. Iron burns skin.
parts.corpo: Revenant opens on collapse: "Slowly creeps, Iron burns skin, Visions tear and absolutes fall." Every certainty gets stripped away before anything is rebuilt.

parts.titolo: Truth bleeds red, freedom fades fast.
parts.corpo: "Truth bleeds red, Freedom fades fast, The Darkness is deep, But spirit stands tall." The collapse is total, except for the one thing the song insists on.

parts.titolo: Taste my blood, rise again.
parts.corpo: "Taste my blood, rise again, serpent sun." Collapse turned into ritual: the wound becomes the exact substance the return is made from.

parts.titolo: Shattered moon, the veil is torn.
parts.corpo: "Shattered moon, the veil is torn, Serpents fill the sky above, Crosses mark the earth below." The whole sky turns into a mirror of what's breaking apart inside.

parts.titolo: Freedom defies death's embrace.
parts.corpo: The line that carries the song: "Freedom defies death's embrace." Not immunity from mortality, defiance of it, chosen again and again.

parts.titolo: And from beginning, the end is known.
parts.corpo: "And from beginning, the end is known." Fatalistic only on the surface: if the ending is certain, meaning lives in how the path gets walked.

parts.titolo: Mortals bow their heads. Defiance burns.
parts.corpo: "Tighten chains, cold, Mortals bow their heads, Defiance burns, Defiant breaths." Obedience is collective. So, the song insists, is the moment someone refuses.

parts.titolo: The rebirth Turning Point was pointing toward.
parts.corpo: Turning Point endures change quietly, over time, in private. Revenant is that same lesson at full volume: total collapse first, then whatever has the nerve to rise out of it. Different pace, same cost.

analyses.caption:
The shortest song says the most.

Dreamer's Sunsets is one suspended line: "Secret dreams, hold my dreams, side by side with you." The dream stops being private the moment it's handed to someone else. That's the risk and the point.

The same words return two tracks later, spoken from the road at midnight: "Secret dreams, hoping morning comes too soon. Hold my dreams as the night turns into day. Side by side with the road, I'll find my way." Not a coincidence: the album keeps circling the same request for company.

A sunset doesn't disappear, it changes color and form. This dream sits on the same threshold: not fulfilled, not lost.

Our reading of the lyrics. Dreamer's Sunsets is track 08 on Roadburn Chronicles. Stream it on Spotify (link in bio).

Who holds your secret dreams?

parts.titolo: Secret dreams, hold my dreams.
parts.corpo: Dreamer's Sunsets is a single suspended line: "Secret dreams, hold my dreams, side by side with you." The whole song lives inside one sentence.

parts.titolo: The dream stops being private.
parts.corpo: To ask someone to hold your dreams is to hand them the most unfinished, most breakable part of yourself. That's the risk, and it's also the entire point.

parts.titolo: Side by side with you.
parts.corpo: "Side by side with you" suggests closeness without possession, two people sharing a direction, not one holding the other.

parts.titolo: A sunset doesn't disappear.
parts.corpo: A sunset doesn't vanish at once, it changes color and form. This dream sits on the exact same threshold: not fulfilled, not lost.

parts.titolo: The same words return, tracks later.
parts.corpo: "Secret dreams, hoping morning comes too soon, Hold my dreams as the night turns into day, Side by side with the road, I'll find my way." Not a coincidence, the album keeps circling this one request.

parts.titolo: One suspended fragment.
parts.corpo: The song is closer to an echo or a remembered vision than a conventional narrative, deliberately brief, deliberately unresolved.

parts.titolo: Two people, one shared horizon.
parts.corpo: By handing the dream over, solitary freedom meets the possibility of companionship. Nothing about this fragment closes the door either way.

parts.titolo: The shortest song, the longest echo.
parts.corpo: This one line returns almost unchanged two tracks later, out on the open road. It's the hinge the album's fourth movement turns on: the same question asked from a bench, a doorway and a moving van. Who do you trust with the parts of you that aren't finished yet?

analyses.caption:
When even the fighting stops, what's left?

Monsters' Conceal doesn't open with anger, it opens with doubt about the past itself: "Your desperate tears, Were they that real?" By the time the song ends, the relationship has run out of even conflict: "So here we stand, With nothing left to say. No angry cries, The hurt we can disguise."

The most desolate line isn't about blame, it's about arithmetic: "In our route There wasn't you and me." And the question that follows is asked together, not apart: "Could it be true, have we become monsters?"

The last verdict offers no relief: "So let it be, The wounds will never heal, A shattered dream, monsters' conceal."

Our reading of the lyrics. Monsters' Conceal is track 09 on Roadburn Chronicles. Stream it on Spotify (link in bio).

What's the quietest way a bond ever ended for you?

parts.titolo: Your desperate tears. Were they that real?
parts.corpo: Monsters' Conceal opens with doubt about the past itself: "Your desperate tears, Were they that real? The silent fears are hard to heal?" Even memory gets re-examined through the damage that followed.

parts.titolo: Are we to blame for losing our light?
parts.corpo: "Though love has turned and dark fills the night, Are we to blame for losing our light?" The plural matters, nobody gets to stand outside the wreckage.

parts.titolo: Have we become monsters?
parts.corpo: "In quiet hours, when old shadows raise, Could it be true, have we become monsters?" Not villain and victim. Both drained by what's left of it.

parts.titolo: There wasn't you and me.
parts.corpo: The most desolate line is about arithmetic, not blame: "The bitter truth, It is now clear to see, In our route, There wasn't you and me."

parts.titolo: No angry cries.
parts.corpo: "So here we stand, With nothing left to say, No angry cries, The hurt we can disguise." Even the fighting has run out, that's how you know it's really over.

parts.titolo: The silence screams too loud.
parts.corpo: "So, in the end, The silence screams too loud, No love to send, No solace need to be found." Anger still holds attachment. Silence is what's left once even that's gone.

parts.titolo: The wounds will never heal.
parts.corpo: The last verdict offers no relief: "So let it be, The wounds will never heal, A shattered dream, monsters' conceal." No absolution, just naming.

parts.titolo: When the record stops arguing.
parts.corpo: Rusty Blues grieves what's already gone. Dreamer's Sunsets hands over something still fragile and unfinished. Monsters' Conceal is a third kind of loss entirely: not death, not distance, just two people who ran out of even the will to fight.

analyses.caption:
Freedom, without the grand gesture.

After the album's heaviest conflicts, An Old Van and a Couple of Beers opens the road: "Open road, Rolling fields beneath the sky." Having "no place I have to be" isn't the same as being lost, it's room to breathe.

The happiness on offer is deliberately small: "An old van and a couple of beers, Laughing through hundred miles with no fears." No luxury, no triumph, just "Living under the stars, now and here." Under an "Endless sky, Feeling small but feeling free."

The past doesn't disappear. "Silent roads, Echoes of my travels past" still travel with him. And by the end, even the road becomes the companion: "Side by side with the road, I'll find my way."

Our reading of the lyrics. Track 10 on Roadburn Chronicles. Stream it on Spotify (link in bio).

Who's in your van?

parts.titolo: Open road, rolling fields beneath the sky.
parts.corpo: After the album's heaviest conflicts, the road opens up: "Open road, Rolling fields beneath the sky, Feeling free, As the world just passes by."

parts.titolo: No place I have to be.
parts.corpo: "Empty lanes, And no place I have to be, Summer breeze, Chasing dreams just being me." Having nowhere to be isn't the same as being lost, it can be room to breathe.

parts.titolo: An old van and a couple of beers.
parts.corpo: "An old van and a couple of beers, Laughing through hundred miles with no fears." No luxury, no triumph. Just company, and that turns out to be enough.

parts.titolo: Living under the stars, now and here.
parts.corpo: "Living under the stars, now and here." The happiness on offer is deliberately small, and deliberately present tense.

parts.titolo: Lonely nights, silent roads.
parts.corpo: "Lonely nights, Underneath a sky so vast, Silent roads, Echoes of my travels past." Freedom doesn't erase solitude. It just changes what the solitude feels like.

parts.titolo: Feeling small but feeling free.
parts.corpo: "Finding peace, In the whispers of the trees, Endless sky, Feeling small but feeling free." Smallness under an immense sky releases the self from being the center of everything.

parts.titolo: Side by side with the road.
parts.corpo: By the end, even the road becomes company: "Hold my dreams, as the night turns into day, Side by side, with the road, I'll find my way."

parts.titolo: Where the album lands.
parts.corpo: After grief, a fractured love and a dream handed to someone else, the record's last stop is the road: nowhere to be, nothing to prove. Roadburn Chronicles doesn't end in triumph. It ends in enough.

journeys.title: The Shadow
journeys.subtitle: Two songs about the parts of yourself you can't outrun: one learns to carry them, one shows what happens when they start driving.
journeys.caption:
Two songs, one shadow.

The Sinner spends its runtime accepting every color it was told to hide: "I'm a sinner, an enemy of God, family ruiner, a demon of my time" becomes, by the end, "And I'm here now, with all my colors, the only one awake among my enemies."

Viper picks up right where that honesty turns dangerous. "My soul is dust, my body is burning, ready or not, the Viper's coming." Same darkness, no longer carried, now craved: "Toxin leaves behind a splinter, sometimes it burn, sometimes it hurt."

Carry your shadow, or let it carry you. Roadburn Chronicles asks the same question twice, from two different distances.

Our reading of the lyrics. The Sinner (track 02) and Viper (track 06) on Roadburn Chronicles. Stream them on Spotify (link in bio).

Which one are you living right now?

movements.cit: I'm a sinner / an enemy of God / Family ruiner / A demon of my time
movements.corpo: The Sinner opens with a list of verdicts that sound like they came from somewhere else, until you notice who is actually speaking them.

movements.titolo: Grey like my skies, purple like my veins.
movements.corpo: "Grey like my skies, and purple like my veins, any color you prefer, they're just a part of me." The self stops being one thing. It becomes a whole palette, contradictions included.

movements.cit: My soul is dust, my body is burning / Ready or not, the Viper's coming
movements.corpo: Viper doesn't open with a stranger's danger. It opens with something that was always inside, finally wide awake.
"My perversion, your innocence are the elements, a lying process in between." Not one villain and one victim: the same shadow The Sinner learned to carry, now something you can crave.

movements.cit: And I'm here now / with all my colors / the only one awake among my enemies
movements.corpo: The turn the whole song was built for. Not triumph over the shadow: permission to carry all of it at once.

movements.cit: Toxin leaves behind a splinter / Sometimes it burn, sometimes it hurt
movements.corpo: Even after acceptance, something stays lodged where the bite was. Roadburn Chronicles never pretends the shadow comes free.

journeys.title: Broken Illusions
journeys.subtitle: Two songs about the certainties we build to feel safe, and what's left once they can't hold weight anymore.
journeys.caption:
Two collapses, same foundation.

S.U.R.E. dismantles the stories we perform for the world: "Pillars of sand, the right, the true, the false and the God, an anthill and the Colosseum." Whole systems of certainty, reduced to something that can't hold weight. "Anger is an acid that can do more harm to the fucking vessel in which it is stored than to anything on which it is poured."

I For An I turns the same blade inward: a civil war between the voice that built those certainties and the one that never bought them. "We have the same fucking weight. One blind, one deaf." The exit isn't more certainty. It's honesty: "I prefer doubt and fear."

Self Utopias Ruins Existence, the title says. I For An I shows exactly whose existence it ruins first.

Our reading of the lyrics. S.U.R.E. (track 01) and I For An I (track 04) on Roadburn Chronicles. Stream them on Spotify (link in bio).

Which certainty are you still protecting?

movements.cit: Do you see light / with your closed eyes? / Are you aware that You're dying
movements.corpo: S.U.R.E. opens with questions that refuse to comfort. Closed eyes, closed ears: certainty, built by shutting the world out.

movements.titolo: Pillars of sand: the right, the true.
movements.corpo: "Pillars of sand, the right, the true, the false and the God, an anthill and the Colosseum." Whole systems of certainty, reduced to something that can't hold weight.

movements.titolo: Careful boy, dreaming of roads and freedom.
movements.corpo: "Careful boy, oh you can't think, dreaming of roads and freedom, wrong about life." The same certainty S.U.R.E. warned about, now speaking from inside one head.

movements.cit: Monochromatic words yeah / You're teaching me / while truth chokes you
movements.corpo: The younger voice answers back: an existence drained of color by inherited formulas. Nobody in this fight is innocent, and nobody is fully wrong.

movements.cit: You're dying in silence / between slaves'n'Rulers
movements.corpo: Picking a side and calling it safety has a cost. It just relocates the silence, the same silence I For An I finds one verse later, inside a single skull.

movements.cit: 'Cause I prefer doubt and fear / I prefer doubt and fear
movements.corpo: The exit from both songs is the same: not a better certainty, just the honesty to admit you don't have one. Doubt keeps the question alive.

journeys.title: The Turning
journeys.subtitle: Change first as something you endure quietly, then as something that has to burn you down before it rebuilds you.
journeys.caption:
Endurance, then collapse, then rise.

Turning Point is change in slow motion: "Compass has been broken for long time," and the shift itself arrives almost silently: "Do you feel it? Your wind is changing." Growth here is "the hardest sowing, the precious yield": paid for in mud and blood, never applauded.

Revenant is the same lesson at full volume. Everything gets stripped away, "Visions tear and absolutes fall," before anything rises: "Taste my blood, rise again, serpent sun." "Freedom defies death's embrace," not by denying the ending, but by choosing to keep walking anyway.

One song teaches you to bend. The other teaches you what happens when you finally break, and rise anyway.

Our reading of the lyrics. Turning Point (track 03) and Revenant (track 07) on Roadburn Chronicles. Stream them on Spotify (link in bio).

What had to fall apart before you changed?

movements.cit: Do you feel it? / Your wind is changing / One single moment / A turning Point
movements.corpo: Nothing around him necessarily moves. The direction does, and that's the whole song.

movements.titolo: The hardest sowing, the precious yield.
movements.corpo: "The hardest sowing, the precious yield, a necessary and lonely hard path, never gratitude." Growth here isn't rewarded. It's paid for, alone, on credit.
Revenant opens where Turning Point's quiet erosion finally gives out completely: "visions tear and absolutes fall." Every certainty stripped away before anything gets rebuilt.

movements.cit: Taste my blood / rise again / serpent sun
movements.corpo: Collapse turned into ritual. The wound becomes the exact substance the return is made from.

movements.cit: It's finally dawn / So much poison'n'mud / An elusive / and shining light
movements.corpo: Dawn doesn't cancel the night that came before it. It proves the night wasn't the whole story.

movements.cit: Freedom defies death's embrace
movements.corpo: The line both songs were building toward. Not immunity from the ending: defiance of it, chosen again and again.

journeys.title: Love, Freedom and Loss
journeys.subtitle: Four songs about the record's quieter conflict: a love that ends, a dream you hand someone, a grief that still gets a toast, and a road that finally lets you breathe.
journeys.caption:
The album's quieter half.

Not every fight on Roadburn Chronicles is loud. Monsters' Conceal ends a relationship without a single angry word: "So here we stand, with nothing left to say. No angry cries, the hurt we can disguise." "In our route there wasn't you and me."

Dreamer's Sunsets hands the most fragile thing over anyway: "Secret dreams, hold my dreams, side by side with you." Rusty Blues keeps a bond alive past the point where it should be possible: "But when night falls and darkness creeps, I sit and I can talk to you."

And An Old Van and a Couple of Beers finally lets the record breathe: "Living under the stars, now and here." Freedom, without the grand gesture.

Our reading of the lyrics. Monsters' Conceal (09), An Old Van and a Couple of Beers (10), Dreamer's Sunsets (08) and Rusty Blues (05) on Roadburn Chronicles. Stream them on Spotify (link in bio).

Which one are you in right now?

movements.cit: So, in the end / The silence screams too loud
movements.corpo: Monsters' Conceal doesn't end in a fight. It ends in the quiet that's left once even the fighting stops.

"Your bench ain't empty anymore, young folks and families pass by." Rusty Blues opens on a different kind of ending, one where the bench fills with strangers but the conversation somehow continues anyway.

movements.cit: Are we to blame for losing our light?
movements.corpo: Not villain and victim: both just drained by what is left of it.
"Side by side with you." Dreamer's Sunsets is a single suspended line: to hand someone your dreams is to hand them the most breakable part of yourself.

movements.cit: A sip of wine / A toast for Father's Day
movements.corpo: A small, repeatable ritual, the kind that keeps a bond honest longer than any big speech could.

movements.titolo: Open road, rolling fields beneath the sky.
movements.corpo: "Feeling free, as the world just passes by." After every ending on this side of the record, the road finally opens.

movements.cit: So let it be / The wounds will never heal / A shattered dream
movements.corpo: No absolution. Just naming, and even that, the record insists, is worth something.

movements.cit: Living under the stars, now and here
movements.corpo: No luxury, no triumph. Just company, and it turns out to be enough. The record's quietest fight ends here: not resolved, just carried gently.

journeys.title: Roadburn Chronicles
journeys.subtitle: The whole arc of the album in one carousel: the illusions that break, the shadow that gets carried, the change that costs before it heals, and the freedom waiting on the other side.
journeys.caption:
The whole record, one thread.

Roadburn Chronicles opens by tearing down the stories we tell ourselves to feel safe ("Self Utopias Ruins Existence"), then asks what's left once you stop hiding the parts of yourself you were taught to hate: "And I'm here now, with all my colors, the only one awake among my enemies."

Change arrives twice: first slow and unheroic ("Do you feel it? Your wind is changing"), then total ("Freedom defies death's embrace"). Love ends without a single raised voice ("No angry cries, the hurt we can disguise"), and the record's last stop is the road, nowhere to be, nothing to prove: "Living under the stars, now and here."

Four dimensions, one voice, one true sentence at the center of all of it: we are here now, with all our colors.

Our reading of the lyrics, across the full album. Roadburn Chronicles, out now. Stream it on Spotify (link in bio).

Which part of this arc are you living?

movements.cit: Do you see light / with your closed eyes? / Are you aware that You're dying
movements.corpo: It starts with the illusions we build to feel safe, and the first crack in each one.

movements.cit: I'm a sinner / an enemy of God / Family ruiner / A demon of my time
movements.corpo: Verdicts that sound like they came from outside, until you notice who is actually speaking them.

movements.cit: Do you feel it? / Your wind is changing / One single moment / A turning Point
movements.corpo: Change, the first time it shows up on this record, arrives almost silently.

movements.cit: Freedom defies death's embrace
movements.corpo: The second time, it arrives as collapse, and a choice to keep walking anyway.

movements.cit: So here we stand / With nothing left to say
movements.corpo: Not every ending on this record is loud. Some just run out of anything left to fight about.

movements.cit: Living under the stars, now and here
movements.corpo: And after all of it: the road. Nowhere to be, nothing to prove, just enough.

movements.cit: And I'm here now / with all my colors / the only one awake among my enemies
movements.corpo: The line the whole album keeps circling back to. Not a resolution: a way of carrying everything that came before it.
